nodes.content: Design a network diagnosis system that separates concurrent causal faults from downstream symptoms under asymmetric routing and incomplete telemetry.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% fault-localization precision at ≥80% incident coverage with 30% telemetry loss.
Report observationally indistinguishable fault sets without asserting unsupported single-cause explanations.

nodes.content: Build asymmetric-path causal factor graphs with missingness-aware telemetry likelihoods and multi-fault inference, separating downstream symptoms and returning indistinguishable fault sets.
How can asymmetric-path factor graphs separate concurrent faults from symptoms and flag indistinguishable fault sets under 30% telemetry loss?
Under 30% telemetry loss, asymmetric-path multi-fault inference achieves ≥90% localization precision at ≥80% coverage, grouping indistinguishable faults while excluding symptoms.
Simulate 10,000 AsymRouteBench incidents with concurrent faults, asymmetric paths, and 30% telemetry loss; measure precision, coverage, ambiguity, and symptom rejection.
AsymRouteBench: 92% localization precision at 83% coverage under 30% loss; 94% symptom rejection; indistinguishable cases returned fault sets.
Adopt missingness-aware multi-fault factor graphs with ambiguity-set outputs; AsymRouteBench exceeds precision and coverage targets under 30% loss.
Implement adopted factor-graph service: ingest directional paths, model telemetry loss, infer concurrent faults, group observational equivalents, and validate on AsymRouteBench.
Implement PathGraph v1 with separate forward and reverse route dependencies and per-sensor dropout likelihoods for missing telemetry.
PathGraph v1 module stores directional route dependencies and sensor dropout likelihoods, emitting factor graphs for multi-fault inference.
Run PathGraph v1 conformance tests on 500 asymmetric topologies with 30% sensor dropout, checking directional dependencies and missingness likelihood calibration.
Across 500 asymmetric topologies, PathGraph v1 preserved 99.8% directional dependencies; dropout likelihood ECE was 0.018 at 30% loss.
Test inference on 2,000 held-out AsymRouteBench incidents at 30% loss; measure precision, coverage, symptom rejection, and unsupported singletons.
Held-out AsymRouteBench: 84% precision at 81% coverage, 86% symptom rejection; 14% of indistinguishable cases received unsupported singletons.
Which posterior-set calibration rule eliminates unsupported singletons in indistinguishable incidents while keeping held-out coverage above 80%?
Group observationally equivalent faults before 95% conformal set calibration to eliminate unsupported singletons while achieving ≥90% precision at ≥80% coverage.
Calibrate 95% conformal equivalence-class sets on 1,000 validation incidents; assess precision, coverage, unsupported singletons on 2,000 held-out AsymRouteBench incidents.
Held-out AsymRouteBench: 95% conformal equivalence-class sets yielded 93% precision at 76% incident coverage, with zero unsupported singletons.
Use observability-stratified conformal thresholds and equivalence-class safeguards to target ≥90% precision, ≥80% coverage, and zero unsupported singletons.
Stratify conformal thresholds by directional observability, enforce ambiguity sets, and retest ≥90% precision and ≥80% coverage at 30% loss.
Implement PathGraph v1 observability strata using directional visibility and dropout likelihoods; calibrate stratum-specific thresholds and enforce ambiguity sets.
StrataCal v1 adds directional-observability thresholds to PathGraph v1 and returns equivalence-class fault sets instead of unsupported singletons.
Does StrataCal v1 restore ≥80% held-out incident coverage at ≥90% precision without unsupported singletons under 30% telemetry loss?
StrataCal v1 achieves ≥90% localization precision at ≥80% incident coverage with zero unsupported singletons on held-out 30%-loss incidents.
Evaluate StrataCal v1 on 2,000 held-out AsymRouteBench incidents at 30% loss; measure localization precision, incident coverage, unsupported singletons.
StrataCal v1 reached 91% localization precision at 79% incident coverage on held-out 30%-loss AsymRouteBench, with zero unsupported singletons.
Run five independent 2,000-incident AsymRouteBench seeds at 30% loss; estimate precision, coverage, and singleton-rate confidence intervals for StrataCal v1.
Five independent seeds: mean precision 91.6% (95% CI 90.7–92.5%), coverage 81.3% (80.4–82.2%); zero unsupported singletons.
Which observability strata caused the 79% coverage run, and can targeted recalibration raise worst-seed coverage without reducing precision?
Low-visibility strata cause the 79% coverage run; targeted recalibration yields ≥80% worst-seed coverage, ≥90% precision, and zero unsupported singletons.
Audit the 79%-coverage run and five seeds by directional visibility; recalibrate low-visibility thresholds, then retest worst-seed precision, coverage, and singletons.
Low-visibility strata accounted for 73% of 79%-run misses; recalibration yielded 80.6% worst-seed coverage, 90.8% precision, zero unsupported singletons.
Independently sweep StrataCal v1 low-visibility thresholds across five new 30%-loss seeds, tracking worst-seed coverage, precision, and unsupported singletons.
Across five new seeds, recalibrated thresholds yielded 79.2% worst-seed coverage, 90.6% precision, and zero unsupported singletons.
Do correlated directional sensor dropouts explain worst-seed coverage below 80%, despite per-sensor missingness calibration?
Correlated directional dropouts drive low-visibility misses; modeling shared failures yields ≥80% worst-seed coverage at ≥90% precision without unsupported singletons.
Audit both StrataCal v1 recalibration runs for correlated low-visibility dropout; retest worst-seed coverage, precision, and singleton rate.
Original-seed recalibration retained 80.6% worst-seed coverage, 90.8% precision, and zero unsupported singletons; correlated dropouts explained 72% of new-seed low-visibility misses.
Add shared-failure latent factors to StrataCal v1; benchmark five fresh 30%-loss seeds for worst-seed coverage, precision, and unsupported singletons.
Five fresh seeds with shared-failure factors yielded 79.7% worst-seed coverage, 91.0% precision, and zero unsupported singletons.
Retune StrataCal v1 shared-dropout factors after 79.7% worst-seed coverage; compare independent-dropout ablation on fresh 30%-loss seeds for coverage, precision, singletons.
Retuned shared-dropout factors achieved 81.1% worst-seed coverage versus 78.9% without them, 90.5% precision, and zero unsupported singletons.
Adopt retuned shared-dropout factors after worst-seed coverage improved from 79.7% to 81.1%, with 90.5% precision and zero unsupported singletons.
Integrate adopted shared-dropout factors; compare correlated-dropout and independent-dropout ablations across 10 fresh seeds, tracking worst-seed coverage, precision, and singletons.
Integrate retuned shared-dropout factors; compare worst-seed coverage, precision, and singleton rate against ablation across 10 fresh 30%-loss seeds.
StrataCal v2 integrates retuned shared-dropout factors and includes 10-seed ablation reports tracking coverage, precision, and unsupported singletons.
Add budgeted directional probes chosen to distinguish concurrent fault sets from downstream symptoms, retaining ambiguity sets when evidence remains insufficient.
Implement entropy-guided directional probes, limited to three per incident; evaluate precision, coverage, and ambiguity reporting under 30% telemetry loss.
Implement StrataCal v2 probe selector ranking directional path tests by expected fault-set information gain, capped at three probes per incident.
ProbeSelect v1 ranks directional tests by expected information gain, requests at most three per incident, and preserves unresolved fault sets.
Do three ProbeSelect v1 directional probes improve localization coverage without lowering precision or inventing singleton causes under 30% telemetry loss?
Three ProbeSelect v1 probes raise worst-seed coverage above 81.1%, retain ≥90% precision, and produce zero unsupported singletons.
Compare ProbeSelect v1 against no probes across 10 fresh AsymRouteBench seeds at 30% loss; record worst-seed coverage, precision, unsupported singletons.
Across 10 fresh seeds, probes raised worst-seed coverage from 81.4% to 84.2%; precision was 90.4%, with zero unsupported singletons.
Run 2,000 asymmetric dual-fault AsymRouteBench incidents at 30% loss; compare probes versus no-probe on symptom rejection and ambiguity-set validity.
On 2,000 dual-fault incidents, probes improved symptom rejection from 89% to 94%; all 136 unresolved cases retained valid ambiguity sets.
Inject 20% probe timeouts into 2,000 30%-loss AsymRouteBench incidents; compare precision, coverage, and ambiguity preservation against no-probe inference.
With 20% probe timeouts, precision fell to 88.7% at 82.3% coverage; ambiguity sets remained valid, but localization missed 90% precision.
Can timeout-aware probe likelihoods restore ≥90% precision at ≥80% coverage when 20% of probes time out?
Model probe timeouts as missing observations, not failed paths, to restore ≥90% precision at ≥80% coverage without unsupported singletons.
Patch ProbeSelect v1 timeout likelihoods; replay e13’s 136 unresolved cases and e14’s timeout cohort, measuring precision, coverage, and singleton validity.
Timeout-aware replay: 90.8% precision, 81.7% coverage at 20% timeouts; zero unsupported singletons, 136 ambiguity sets preserved.
Freeze replay-validated timeout-aware likelihoods; test five fresh 30%-loss AsymRouteBench seeds with 20% probe timeouts for precision, coverage, unsupported singletons.
Five fresh seeds with 20% probe timeouts yielded 89.3% worst-seed precision at 81.0% coverage, with zero unsupported singletons.
Gate probe-assisted localization during timeouts: replay passed, but fresh-seed precision fell below 90%; return calibrated ambiguity sets instead.
Implement timeout-triggered probe gating with StrataCal v2 ambiguity-set fallback; retest five fresh seeds for precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Implement timeout-gated ProbeSelect v1 with StrataCal v2 ambiguity fallback; retest five fresh 30%-loss seeds at 20% timeouts.
ProbeSelect v1.1 gates timeout-affected probe evidence, falls back to StrataCal v2 ambiguity sets, and includes five-seed timeout regression tests.
Test ProbeSelect v1.1 across five dual-fault AsymRouteBench seeds at 30% loss, 20% timeouts; measure precision, coverage, unsupported singletons.
Five dual-fault seeds: worst-seed precision 90.3%, coverage 80.4% at 30% loss and 20% timeouts; 93% symptom rejection, zero unsupported singletons.
Adopt timeout-gated ProbeSelect v1.1: worst-seed precision reached 90.3%, coverage 80.4%, with zero unsupported singletons at 20% probe timeouts.
